scored_cells.answer_excerpt:
To get your website cited by AI search engines, think less “trick the AI” and more **become the clearest, most trustworthy, easiest-to-retrieve source for specific questions**. AI citations usually come from the same ingredients as strong SEO: crawlability, authority, clarity, topical depth, and useful original information.

Here’s a practical checklist.

## 1. Make sure AI/search crawlers can access your site

If AI systems can’t crawl your pages, they can’t cite them.

Check your `robots.txt` and firewall/CDN rules. At minimum, do **not accidentally block** major search crawlers or AI search crawlers you want visibility from.

For Google AI Overviews, Google says normal SEO fundamentals still apply and that you do **not** need a special “AI file,” special markup, or separate opt-in to appear in AI features. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features?utm_source=openai))

For ChatGPT Search, OpenAI says publishers may need to allow **OAI-SearchBot** in `robots.txt`; it also distinguishes search access from training access, so you can allow search discovery without necessarily allowing all training crawlers. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12627856-publishers-and-developers-faq%23%3A~%3Atext%3DChatGPT%20automatically%20includes%20the%20UTM%20parameter%20utm_source%3Dchatgpt.com%20in%20referral%20URLs%2C%20enabling%20clear%20tracking%20and%20analysis%20of%20inbound%20traffic%20from%20ChatGPT%20search%20result

**Generative Engine Optimization, or GEO,** is the practice of making your brand, website, products, and expertise more likely to be **found, understood, cited, summarized, or recommended by AI answer engines** such as Google AI Overviews/AI Mode, ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, Copilot, and similar systems.

In plain English: **SEO helps you rank in search results. GEO helps you show up inside AI-generated answers.**

Google’s current guidance is important here: for Google Search’s AI features, the fundamentals of good SEO still matter, and Google explicitly warns against chasing “AEO/GEO hacks” like unnecessary `llms.txt` files or artificial tactics. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide?authuser=4&hl=en&utm_source=openai))

## How GEO differs from traditional SEO

| Traditional SEO | Generative Engine Optimization |
|---|---|
| Goal: rank pages in search results | Goal: be cited, summarized, or recommended in AI answers |
| Focuses on keywords, links, crawlability, relevance | Focuses on clarity, authority, answer quality, entity recognition, structured information |
| Users click a result and read | Users may get a synthesized answer before clicking |
| Success metric: rankings, impressions, traffic | Success metric: AI mentions, citations, referral traffic, share of answer, accuracy of representation |

scored_cells.answer_excerpt:
**Short answer: yes, but mostly indirectly — schema markup is not a magic “get cited by AI” switch.**

Adding schema can help AI/search systems understand your content, entities, authorship, products, FAQs, reviews, locations, and relationships more clearly. But current evidence suggests **schema alone does not reliably increase AI citations** in Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Copilot.

Google’s own documentation frames structured data as a way to help Google understand pages and make them eligible for rich results, not as a guaranteed ranking or AI-citation factor. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/search-gallery?authuser=2&utm_source=openai)) Bing similarly says structured data gives Bing valuable information about the type of content on a site, while its AI reporting focuses on broader citation/visibility patterns rather than schema as a direct lever. ([bing.com](https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/marking-up-your-site-with-structured-data-3a93e731?country=69&utm_source=openai))

The practical view:

### What schema **can** help with

- **Clarifying entities**: Organization, Person, Product, LocalBusiness, Article, FAQPage, HowTo, Event, Review, etc.
- **Making your content easier to parse** for crawlers.
- **Supporting rich results** in traditional search.
- **Reinforcing trust signals** like author, datePublished, dateModified, sameAs, logo, address, aggregateRating, offers, and citations

## What is Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)?

**Answer Engine Optimization** is the practice of making your content easy for AI-powered search tools and “answer engines” to understand, trust, extract, and cite as a direct answer.

Traditional SEO focuses on ranking web pages in search results. **AEO focuses on being the answer** in places like:

- Google AI Overviews
- Featured snippets
- Bing Copilot
- Perplexity
- ChatGPT with web/search retrieval
- Gemini
- Voice assistants
- “People also ask” style results

AEO overlaps heavily with SEO, but the goal is slightly different: instead of only trying to get a blue-link ranking, you’re trying to make your brand, page, product, or expertise the source an answer engine uses when responding to a user’s question. Recent AEO guides generally define it as structuring content, entity data, and authority signals so AI systems can retrieve and cite your content in generated answers. ([aisearchvisibility.ai](https://www.aisearchvisibility.ai/answer-engine-optimization?utm_source=openai))

---

## The simple version

If SEO asks:

> “How do I rank for this keyword?”

AEO asks:

> “When someone asks a question, how do I become the answer?”

Example:

Search query: **“How long does dental bonding last?”**

An SEO-focused page might have a title like:

> Dental Bonding Services in Austin | Smith Family Dental

Here’s a practical plan.

## 1. Start with normal SEO fundamentals

AI search still depends heavily on conventional search infrastructure: crawlability, indexability, authority, relevance, and structured content. Google says its AI search systems rely on the same basic ways Google Search finds and processes pages, so foundational SEO still matters. ([developers.google.cn](https://developers.google.cn/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide?hl=en&utm_source=openai))

- Make sure important pages are **indexable**.
- Submit XML sitemaps.
- Fix broken pages, redirect chains, duplicate canonicals, and thin pages.
- Use fast, mobile-friendly pages.
- Write clear title tags and meta descriptions.
- Build topical internal links.
- Earn authoritative backlinks and mentions.
- Use HTTPS.
- Make sure your content is actually visible in HTML, not hidden behind scripts.
